transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-11 16:00 UTC | Duration ~62 mins | Record: Yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Dunn (Redwood CSM); Evelyn Harper (Northstar CTO), Marco Ruiz (Head of ML), Sana Abbasi (Security Architect), Oliver Chen (PM)
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll run for about an hour. quick round of intros?
Evelyn Harper: Evelyn—CTO at Northstar. We're running a few pilots across claims automation and policy QA.
Marco Ruiz: Marco, head of ML; I'll own evaluation and perf on our side.
Sana Abbasi: Sana, security architect. I'll be the main interface for compliance and controls.
Oliver Chen: Oliver, product — I'll coordinate acceptance criteria.
Jordan Lee: Great. Priya and Marcus from my side. Today: align on security requirements for the POC and the benchmark plan. We'll also capture success criteria and timeline.
[03:12] Priya Kapoor: Quick agenda, we want to cover access model (SSO/SAML, SCIM), RBAC roles, audit logging, key management, plus the benchmark workload — tokens per request, concurrent sessions, and latency SLOs. Any additional must-haves?
Sana Abbasi: Data residency and PII handling are required up front. Northstar must ensure no raw PII is stored beyond the retention window. Also we run under strict contracts — SOC 2 and ISO are baseline.
Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We can share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 scope. We'll also note our private deployment options; for the pilot you can choose hosted with VPC peering or Dedicated capacity.
[08:45] Marco Ruiz: For the workload, typical request size: nightly batch of 15k requests for summarization, but interactive product flows are smaller — median 120 tokens in, ~80 tokens out; peak concurrency for product is about 30 concurrent users which maps to roughly 25 req/s during spikes. We want to validate p95 latency under load and token cost.
Priya Kapoor: Helpful. When you say "token cost" do you mean cost per token or quality/regression vs your current in-house?
Marco Ruiz: Both. We have an in-house optimized runtime but it's expensive to maintain. We want inference accuracy parity plus 20–30% cost savings ideally.
Sana Abbasi: On controls: we need SSO with SAML, SCIM provisioning for users, RBAC that supports at minimum: Admin, Dev, Audit, Read-only. Also we need exportable audit logs (immutable format) for 12 months and the ability to push logs to our SIEM.
[14:30] Jordan Lee: For SSO/SAML and SCIM — Redwood supports SAML 2.0; we can do IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. SCIM provisioning is available in Dedicated and Private modes today, and we're adding SCIM to hosted tenants next quarter — Priya, correct?
Priya Kapoor: Yeah, hosted SCIM is slated but for the pilot we can enable SCIM on a Dedicated sandbox; alternatively we can do manual provisioning if timing is tight.
Oliver Chen: Can you do Just-In-Time provisioning? That's part of our identity flow.
Priya Kapoor: We can support JIT for SAML assertions; we need to confirm mapping to RBAC groups — I'll follow up with the mapping doc.
Sana Abbasi: KMS is critical: we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for any persisted artifacts and audit logs. Is BYOK supported on hosted?
Jordan Lee: BYOK is available for Private deployments and Dedicated with HSM-backed KMS integrations; for hosted we offer provider-managed KMS but can do field-level encryption and token redaction. We can run the POC in a Dedicated sandbox to meet KMS and SCIM requirements.
[21:10] Marco Ruiz: For acceptance criteria on performance: we need p95 latency <= 250 ms for chat-style calls at 100-token sequences, and sustained throughput of 30 requests/sec for the interactive flow while processing the nightly batch at 15k requests in a 2-hour window. Also no more than 1% error rate.
Priya Kapoor: We'll design a benchmark that mimics that: mix of interactive requests and batch ingestion. We'll need sample prompts and traces from you to make it realistic.
Evelyn Harper: On compliance, besides SOC2 and ISO, we require monthly access reviews for accounts in the pilot and a runbook for incident response integration. Also, do you provide audit log export in near-real time to our SIEM (Splunk)?
Jordan Lee: Yes, audit log streaming to S3 or direct SIEM integration via forwarder is supported. Logs include request metadata, user IDs, model version and response size. We'll provide log schema in the security pack.
[29:00] Sana Abbasi: A couple of red flags we've seen from vendors: logs that don't include model version, or that redact too aggressively, which hinders debugging. We need full traceability — at least for the pilot — and the ability to mark PII fields in logs.
Priya Kapoor: Understood. For traceability we capture model hash, run-time flags (quantization profile, batching window) and the exact prompt payload (if permitted). For PII, we can enable automatic redaction before persistence; we can also keep raw payloads in a restricted-only-access store for a short retention window if you need that for debugging.
Marco Ruiz: That short window — what does "short" mean? We need to know retention numbers to align with policy.
Jordan Lee: Default retention for payloads is 7 days in hosted; in Dedicated/Private you can configure retention or route to your KMS-backed storage. For the POC we can set retention to 3 days and push logs to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules.
[36:45] Oliver Chen: On RBAC, can we scope per-customer and per-project roles? We have multiple internal teams and need to limit access to specific datasets.
Priya Kapoor: Yes, we support project-scoped roles and API key scoping to projects/environments. We'll send the RBAC matrix; you can map your groups to Redwood roles via SCIM group sync.
Sana Abbasi: Do you support session-based audit trails? e.g., tie a specific API key/session to a user identity for investigations.
Jordan Lee: Yes, session linkage is included if you enable SSO and pass the user identifier. For API-key-only flows we recommend short-lived keys or token exchange via our OAuth flow.
[44:20] Marco Ruiz: Back to benchmarks — we also want to test variability with longer sequences: up to 1024 tokens for multi-document summarization. Latency will obviously increase, but we want to measure per-token cost and effective throughput for those jobs.
Priya Kapoor: We'll include a long-sequence profile; for the multi-doc summarization we'll test with a batch micro-burst profile to emulate peak concurrency during nightly jobs. We'll run both single-node and scaled runs to show linearity.
Evelyn Harper: Security-wise, do you do periodic penetration tests and vulnerability disclosures? We need to know cadence and if we can run coordinated tests during POC.
Jordan Lee: We have quarterly pentests and an internal vuln program; we can coordinate a limited scope test during the pilot — we'd need a test plan and a time window. We'll share our contact for coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
[52:10] Sana Abbasi: Regarding certifications, can you share the scope of your SOC 2 — what systems are in-scope (control plane, runtime, telemetry)? Also ISO2658 — sorry ISO27001 — the scope and last audit date.
Jordan Lee: We'll share the SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation; SOC2 covers the control plane, runtime, and telemetry pipelines. ISO audit was completed in Q2 2026. I'll attach the redacted reports.
Marcus Dunn: Note: we'll redact service account identifiers before sharing publicly; sensitive items will be shared over the secure artifact link.
Marco Ruiz: One practical question — model variants and graceful fallback. If you run out of capacity in Dedicated sandbox, do you fall back to a smaller quantized model automatically? We need deterministic behavior for SLAs.
Priya Kapoor: We have policy-based routing. For the POC we can pin to a specific model family; automatic fallback to smaller variants is configurable or disabled. We'll show how rollback and canarying works in the console.
[59:50] Jordan Lee: To recap: agreed pilot scope is 4 weeks — provisioning (week 1), baseline runs and access controls (week 2), scaled benchmarks and security testing (week 3), acceptance and handoff (week 4). Success criteria: p95 latency <= 250 ms for interactive flow, throughput 30 req/s sustained, error rate <1%, SOC2/ISO evidence and SSO+SCIM enabled, audit log streaming to SIEM, and KMS customer-managed key for persisted artifacts. Action owners and dates noted in the chat.
Evelyn Harper: That timeline looks good. We need the SOC2 docs and benchmark plan by Friday.
Jordan Lee: You'll have them by Friday EOD. Priya will send the benchmark harness. Marcus will provision the tenant and set up the SSO test account.
Sana Abbasi: We'll send our PII constraints and retention policy. Expect a legal review after we see the SOC2 artifacts.
Jordan Lee: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark run.
[END]
